Parties: we represent Corio Inc.; counterparty is Commerce One, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: 14.9 Bankruptcy. The parties hereto agree that Corio, as a licensee of Commerce One's intellectual property, shall be afforded all of the protections afforded to a licensee under Section 365(n) of the United States Bankruptcy Code
input.rationale:
A full-text search for "insurance" returns only the Net Revenue definition (p0012); neither the Miscellaneous section (14.1–14.10) nor the Indemnification section contains any insurance covenant, so no clause meets even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). Commerce One is a vendor that touches our data and premises: it supplies an on-site operations consultant and professional services (Sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.6) and operates the MarketSite.net Service used by Corio and its Customers, so the absence of insurance is walk-away territory under the rule. Proposed insertion of a new Section 14.10 in Miscellaneous at the preferred limits (USD 1M/2M CGL, USD 2M E&O, USD 5M cyber, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), with the fallback limits offered in the comment; existing 14.10 renumbers.</parationale>
<parameter name="confidence">0.86

ops.text: 14.10 Insurance. Commerce One shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) where Commerce One processes Corio or Customer data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Commerce One shall provide Corio with certificates of insurance upon request.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance covenant even though Commerce One places consultants on site and its MarketSite.net Service handles Corio and Customer data, so we have added our standard insurance provision (USD 1M/2M CGL, USD 2M E&O, USD 5M cyber, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request) and the following subsection renumbers. If these limits are an issue, we can fall back to USD 1,000,000 errors and omissions and USD 2,000,000 cyber liability coverage.
proposal.summary: Insert vendor insurance covenant (CGL, E&O, cyber) as new Section 14.10

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Corio Inc.; counterparty is Commerce One, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

input.rationale:
A full-text search for "insurance" returns only the Net Revenue definition (p0012); neither the Miscellaneous section (14.1–14.10) nor the Indemnification section contains any insurance covenant, so no clause meets even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). Commerce One is a vendor that touches our data and premises: it supplies an on-site operations consultant and professional services (Sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.6) and operates the MarketSite.net Service used by Corio and its Customers, so the absence of insurance is walk-away territory under the rule. system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Corio Inc.; counterparty is Commerce One, Inc..

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Parties: we represent Corio Inc.; counterparty is Commerce One, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: 14.9 Bankruptcy. The parties hereto agree that Corio, as a licensee of Commerce One's intellectual property, shall be afforded all of the protections afforded to a licensee under Section 365(n) of the United States Bankruptcy Code
input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns only the Net Revenue definition (p0012); neither the Miscellaneous section (14.1-14.10) nor the Indemnification section contains any insurance covenant, so no clause meets even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). Commerce One is a vendor that touches our data and premises: it supplies an on-site operations consultant and professional services (Sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.6) and operates the MarketSite.net Service used by Corio and its Customers, so the absence of insurance is walk-away territory under the rule. Proposed insertion of a new Section 14.10 in Miscellaneous at the preferred limits (USD 1M/2M CGL, USD 2M E&O, USD 5M cyber, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), with the fallback limits offered in the comment; the existing 14.10 renumbers.

ops.text: 14.10 Insurance. Commerce One shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) where Commerce One processes Corio or Customer data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Commerce One shall provide Corio with certificates of insurance upon request.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance covenant even though Commerce One places consultants on site and its MarketSite.net Service handles Corio and Customer data, so we have added our standard insurance provision (USD 1M/2M CGL, USD 2M E&O, USD 5M cyber, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request) and the following subsection renumbers. If these limits are an issue, we can fall back to USD 1,000,000 errors and omissions and USD 2,000,000 cyber liability coverage.
proposal.summary: Insert vendor insurance covenant (CGL, E&O, cyber) as new Section 14.10

input.rationale:
A full-text search for "insurance" returns only the Net Revenue definition (p0012); neither the Miscellaneous section (14.1–14.10) nor the Indemnification section contains any insurance covenant, so no clause meets even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). Commerce One is a vendor that touches our data and premises: it supplies an on-site operations consultant and professional services (Sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.6) and operates the MarketSite.net Service used by Corio and its Customers, so the absence of insurance is walk-away territory under the rule. Proposed insertion of a new Section 14.10 in Miscellaneous at the preferred limits (USD 1M/2M CGL, USD 2M E&O, USD 5M cyber, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), with the fallback limits offered in the comment; existing 14.10 renumbers.</parationale>

input.quote: 4.1 License Fees. In consideration for the licenses granted to Corio pursuant to Section 2 of this Agreement, Corio shall pay the license fees specified in EXHIBIT B hereto.
input.rationale: No minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay or shortfall penalty is imposed on Corio. Fees are limited to (i) the licence fees for the licences actually granted (§4.1, Exhibit B), (ii) annual maintenance and MarketSite.net access fees for services actually provided (§4.2, Exhibit B Payment Terms), (iii) implementation fees on a time-and-materials basis capped by the Statement of Work, and (iv) revenue-share on a percentage of Application Management Revenue actually invoiced to Corio Customers (p0157–p0159) — i.e. usage/ordered-services pricing, which meets the preferred position. Maintenance is expressly conditional ("provided that Corio continues to pay the annual Maintenance and Support fees"), so there is no committed multi-year spend. Two minor points noted but not flagged: the revenue-share carve-out for the initial 3000 user licences is "subject to a minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer" (p0158), which is a counting convention for the free-of-revenue-share pool rather than a purchase commitment on us; and the five-year initial term in §11.1 has no convenience exit, which is a term-length point addressed under the term/termination rule rather than a take-or-pay commitment here. The "shortfall" reference in §4.4 is a mutual audit true-up, not a penalty.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

input.quote: 4.1 License Fees. In consideration for the licenses granted to Corio pursuant to Section 2 of this Agreement, Corio shall pay the license fees specified in EXHIBIT B hereto.
input.rationale: No minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay or shortfall penalty is imposed on Corio. Fees are limited to (i) the licence fees for the licences actually granted (§4.1, Exhibit B), (ii) annual maintenance and MarketSite.net access fees for services actually provided (§4.2, Exhibit B Payment Terms), (iii) implementation fees on a time-and-materials basis capped by the Statement of Work, and (iv) revenue-share on a percentage of Application Management Revenue actually invoiced to Corio Customers (p0157–p0159) — i.e. usage/ordered-services pricing, which meets the preferred position. Maintenance is expressly conditional ("provided that Corio continues to pay the annual Maintenance and Support fees"), so there is no committed multi-year spend. Two minor points noted but not flagged: the revenue-share carve-out for the initial 3000 user licences is "subject to a minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer" (p0158), which is a counting convention for the free-of-revenue-share pool rather than a purchase commitment on us; and the five-year initial term in §11.1 has no convenience exit, which is a term-length point addressed under the term/termination rule rather than a take-or-pay commitment here. The "shortfall" reference in §4.4 is a mutual audit true-up, not a penalty.

ops.text: 11.4 Transition Assistance and Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Commerce One shall (a) at Corio's request, provide reasonable transition assistance to Corio and its Customers for a period of up to six (6) months at Commerce One's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Corio's request, return or make available to Corio all data of Corio, its Customers and Software Users then residing in the Software, the MarketSite.net Service or Commerce One's systems, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Corio in writing. This Section 11.4 shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Corio Inc.; counterparty is Commerce One, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: MISSING — no vendor insurance clause (severity: low).**

- A full-document search for "insurance" surfaced only the Net Revenue definition (p0012); Sections 14 (Miscellaneous) and 8 (Indemnification) contain no insurance covenant, so the clause fails even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).
- Commerce One is squarely within the rule's scope: it places an on-site operations consultant and professional services personnel with Corio (Sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.6) and operates the MarketSite.net Service through which Corio and Customer data flows — i.e., a vendor touching our data and premises, which the playbook treats as walk-away territory when uninsured.
- Redline validated (ok:true) and submitted: a new **Section 14.10 Insurance** inserted after the Bankruptcy provision (p0132) at the preferred limits — USD 1M/2M CGL, USD 2M E&O, USD 5M cyber where Corio/Customer data is processed, statutory workers' comp, certificates on request, maintained through the term plus one year. The comment flags the USD 1M E&O / USD 2M cyber fallback and notes that the existing 14.10 renumbers.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall penalty, or volume cap on Corio:

- **§4.1 / Exhibit B** — licence fees are consideration for the licences actually granted; **§4.2** maintenance is expressly conditional ("provided that Corio continues to pay"), so no committed multi-year spend.
- **Exhibit B Revenue Sharing (p0157–p0159)** — a percentage of Application Management Revenue *actually invoiced* to Corio Customers, with Professional Service and Network access fees excluded; pure usage-based pricing.
- **Exhibit B Implementation Fees** — time-and-materials, capped per the Statement of Work.
- **§4.4** — the word "shortfall" appears only in the mutual audit true-up ("the appropriate party shall promptly pay the amount of such shortfall or refund such overpayment"), which is a true-up, not a penalty.

This sits at the **preferred** position, not merely the fallback.

Two points noted in the rationale but not flagged:
1. The revenue-share carve-out for the initial 3000 user licences is "subject to a minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer" — a counting convention governing the fee-free pool, not a commitment to buy.
2. §11.1's five-year initial term has no convenience exit. That is a term-length issue for the term/termination rule; flagging it here would double-count the same commercial term.

input.quote: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.
input.rationale: Section 11 contains term, termination and survival provisions but no post-termination transition assistance or data return/export obligation. Section 11.3 addresses only mutual return or destruction of Confidential Information (with a Corio carve-out) and continuity of Corio's sublicense rights and Commerce One's support obligations; Section 12's source code escrow provides some continuity of the Software but says nothing about returning Corio's or its Customers' data in a usable format, timing, or certified deletion. In a hosted arrangement where Commerce One operates the MarketSite.net Service, this falls short even of the fallback (90 days of assistance plus 30-day data export), so we insert a new Section 11.4 at the preferred position (up to six months of assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion), with the 90-day fallback available in negotiation.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Corio Inc.; counterparty is Commerce One, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.summary: Insert Section 11.4 requiring Commerce One to provide transition assistance and return Corio/Customer data on termination
input.comment: [Playbook] We have added a transition and data-return provision: on expiry or termination Commerce One provides up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, returns our and our Customers' data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and certifies deletion thereafter. Our playbook requires an orderly exit and return of our data; we can accept 90 days of assistance if six months is not workable.

ops.text: 11.4 Transition Assistance and Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Commerce One shall (a) at Corio's request, provide reasonable transition assistance to Corio and its Customers for a period of up to six (6) months at Commerce One's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Corio's request, return or make available to Corio all data of Corio, its Customers and Software Users then residing in the Software, the MarketSite.net Service or Commerce One's systems, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Corio in writing. This Section 11.4 shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement.

input.rationale: Section 11 contains term, termination and survival provisions but no post-termination transition assistance or data return/export obligation. Section 11.3 addresses only mutual return or destruction of Confidential Information (with a Corio carve-out) and continuity of Corio's sublicense rights and Commerce One's support obligations; Section 12's source code escrow provides some continuity of the Software but says nothing about returning Corio's or its Customers' data in a usable format, timing, or certified deletion. In a hosted arrangement where Commerce One operates the MarketSite.net Service, this falls short even of the fallback (90 days of assistance plus 30-day data export), so we insert a new Section 11.4 at the preferred position (up to six months of assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion), with the 90-day fallback available in negotiation.

**Finding submitted: `missing` (medium severity) — TRANSITION**

**What I checked:**
- **§11 (Term and Termination)** — contains term, breach/insolvency termination, and survival, but no exit mechanics. §11.3 only requires each party to "return or destroy any Confidential Information," with a helpful carve-out letting Corio retain what it needs to support existing Customers.
- **§12 (Source Code Escrow)** — provides Software continuity on release conditions, but nothing about returning Corio's or its Customers' data, format, timing, or deletion.
- Searches for "data," "transition," "migration" returned no export/return obligation anywhere in the document.

**Direction check:** Commerce One hosts the MarketSite.net Service that Corio and its Customers access, so the data-return obligation runs against the counterparty and benefits us — appropriate to insert.

**Classification:** Fails even the fallback (90 days assistance + 30-day export), since no transition or data-return obligation exists at all. Inserted new **§11.4** at the preferred position: up to six (6) months of transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return in a commonly used machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter, with an express survival hook. Redline validated `ok:true`; the 90-day fallback is flagged in the comment as a negotiation concession.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Commerce One / Corio)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Corio)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Commerce One agreement — 18 rules assessed

## Executive summary

The risk is concentrated in four places. First, Section 13.5 flips ownership of Developments Corio creates to Commerce One wherever Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, with no licence back — an assignment of our IP to the vendor. Second, the Section 9 cap is measured by amounts paid "for the transaction which the liability relates to" and carries no carve-out for confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud. Third, Section 11 commits us to a five-year term with no convenience exit. Fourth, there is no vendor insurance covenant and no post-termination transition or data-return obligation in a hosted arrangement. Licence scope (Corio only, no affiliates or contractors) and the 60-day warranty that expires at or before acceptance are the remaining redlines.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 8 Indemnification | One-way vendor IP indemnity, uncapped via the Section 9 carve-out; exceeds fallback on the cap point. Scope is IP-only. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13.5 Shared Resources | "Unless" carve-out transfers Corio-created Developments to Commerce One where it provides ongoing support, with no licence back; fails the fallback. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 9 Limitation of Liability | Cap tied to a single transaction's fees; only carve-out is Section 8. Fails fallback on both cap basis and carve-outs. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 14.1 Miscellaneous | Mutual with an M&A carve-out, but consent is unfettered and there is no affiliate carve-out. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 Grant of Rights | Perpetual and irrevocable, but licences run to "Corio" only; no affiliates or contractors, and § 2.7 bars other access. |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 11 Term and Termination | Five-year term with automatic renewals; § 11.2 triggers limited to uncured breach and insolvency. No convenience exit for us. |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 2 Grant of Rights | All licences non-exclusive; no sole-supplier covenant. Exhibit D cooperation is expressly non-binding. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 2 Grant of Rights | § 2.7 is licence-scope only; § 13.6 preserves independent development. |
| 9 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 4 Fees | No penalty, late interest, shortfall or exit fee payable by Corio. |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 7 Warranties and Disclaimer | Remedy structure is fine, but the 60-day / 31 Dec 1999 window expires at or before acceptance testing; no services warranty. |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 11 Term and Termination | § 11.3 covers Confidential Information only; no data return, format, timing or deletion obligation in a hosted model. |
| 12 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 4.4 Fees | Once yearly, independent CPA acceptable to us, vendor-funded below a 5% threshold, records only. Notice is "reasonable" rather than fixed. |
| 13 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (fallback) | § 14.3 Miscellaneous | California law, AAA in San Francisco. Within the fallback list; we prefer New York courts. |
| 14 | Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 4 Fees | No most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation anywhere. |
| 15 | Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant | § 4 Fees | Fees track licences granted, services provided and revenue actually invoiced; no take-or-pay. |
| 16 | Medium | NOSOLICIT | Compliant | § 13 Shared Resources | No non-solicit or no-hire covenant binding Corio. |
| 17 | Medium | RENEWAL | Compliant | § 11.1 Term and Termination | One-year renewals with a mutual 30-day non-renewal notice. No reminder obligation and no uplift cap (and no uplift right). |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14 Miscellaneous | No insurance covenant at all, despite on-site personnel (§§ 5.1, 5.2, 5.6) and vendor-operated MarketSite.net. |

## Walk-away items

Four findings fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **§ 13.5 — vendor ownership of our Developments.** The support-linked carve-out assigns Customer IP to the vendor with no licence back. Smallest fix is deletion of the carve-out; if Commerce One needs rights in Developments it maintains, a licence from Corio is the sensible landing zone.
2. **§ 9 — per-transaction liability cap and absent carve-outs.** The cap must move to an aggregate 12 months' fees paid or payable (we have proposed the greater of that and US$1,000,000) with carve-outs for breach of confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. The US$1,000,000 floor can be dropped if the carve-outs are accepted.
3. **§ 11 — no customer termination for convenience across a five-year term.** We have proposed a new § 11.3 giving Corio a 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirming Commerce One has no mid-term convenience exit; 60–90 days is the fallback.
4. **§ 14 — no vendor insurance.** Commerce One touches our data and our premises. We have proposed a new § 14.10 at the preferred limits (CGL US$1M/2M, E&O US$2M, cyber US$5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), with fallback limits (E&O US$1M / cyber US$2M) available.

## Next steps

1. Issue the redlines on the six deviations and two missing rules: § 13.5 (delete ownership carve-out), § 9 (cap basis and carve-outs), § 14.1 (affiliate carve-out plus reasonableness standard), § 2 (extend licences to affiliates and contractors, with Corio responsible for compliance), § 11.3 (convenience right), § 11.4 (transition assistance and data return), § 7 (12-month warranty from acceptance, removing the 31 December 1999 cut-off, plus a professional and workmanlike services warranty), and § 14.10 (insurance, renumbering the existing § 14.10).
2. Confirm with the business the value of the affected transactions so we can defend the aggregate cap basis and the US$1,000,000 floor.
3. Identify which Developments Corio expects to create and which Commerce One would support on an ongoing basis, to scope the § 13.5 negotiation and any licence-back.
4. Note for the record, without redlining: the Section 8 indemnity is IP-only with a pro-rated refund; there is no renewal reminder or renewal price-increase cap; § 4.4 audit notice is "reasonable" rather than fixed and the auditor is not expressly bound by confidentiality; and the disclaimer text appears truncated in this copy — we should confirm the full text before signature.
5. Flag that ownership of enhancements to the Software itself is left to future negotiation in the final sentence of § 13.5; the business should decide whether to press that now."}
